events.title: The death of Pope Clement XIV
events.shortBlurb: Ganganelli, the Franciscan pope whom the Bourbon courts pressed to destroy the Jesuits, died at Rome amid rumors the evidence has never sustained…
body: Giovanni Vincenzo Antonio Ganganelli, born at Santarcangelo near Rimini in 1705, a Conventual Franciscan named in religion Lorenzo, rose by learning and modesty to the cardinalate in 1759 and, in May 1769, to the tiara as Clement XIV — chosen after a conclave in which the ambassadors of France and Spain had labored openly.

Those courts, with Naples and Portugal behind them, demanded one thing: the extinction of the Society of Jesus. After four years of resistance and delay, on 21 July 1773, Clement signed the brief Dominus ac Redemptor, suppressing the Society for the peace of the Church throughout the world.

He outlived the deed by fourteen months, dying at Rome on 22 September 1774 after weeks of wasting illness. That the Jesuits had poisoned him was the whisper of all Europe; no evidence has ever sustained it. He was buried in the church of the Twelve Apostles, and the order he had cut down lay in its grave until Pius VII raised it up again in 1814.
